chapters.title: Recipe: accounts
chapters.subtitle: Signup, login, logout and password reset
chapters.summary: A complete, small account flow using Django's built-in auth forms and views, with the settings and templates that make it work.
chapters.quick_answer: Use `UserCreationForm` for signup, the built-in `LoginView`/`LogoutView`/password-reset views for the rest, and `login_required` for private pages. Add email verification only when the product needs it.

sections.title: URLs and settings
sections.body: Wire the built-in views and set the redirect targets. Templates live in `registration/` by convention.
sections.code:
# config/urls.py
from django.contrib.auth import views as auth_views
from django.urls import path
from accounts import views

urlpatterns = [
    path("signup/", views.signup, name="signup"),
    path("login/", auth_views.LoginView.as_view(), name="login"),
    path("logout/", auth_views.LogoutView.as_view(), name="logout"),
    path("password-reset/", auth_views.PasswordResetView.as_view(), name="password_reset"),
    path("password-reset/done/", auth_views.PasswordResetDoneView.as_view(), name="password_reset_done"),
    path("reset/<uidb64>/<token>/", auth_views.PasswordResetConfirmView.as_view(), name="password_reset_confirm"),
    path("reset/done/", auth_views.PasswordResetCompleteView.as_view(), name="password_reset_complete"),
]

LOGIN_URL = "login"
LOGIN_REDIRECT_URL = "home"
LOGOUT_REDIRECT_URL = "home"

sections.title: Signup form and view
sections.body: `UserCreationForm` handles password hashing and validation. Add an email field if you need one, and log the user in after signup.
sections.note: If email is your login identifier, use a custom user model or a custom authentication backend. The default `User` logs in with username.

sections.title: Protect private pages
sections.body: Use `login_required` on function views and `LoginRequiredMixin` on class-based views. Keep the `next` redirect safe.
sections.note: Validate `next` with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme` before redirecting. An open redirect is a phishing primitive.

pitfalls: Using the default user when email is the login identifier.
No email backend, so reset emails never arrive.
checklist: Signup hashes passwords through the auth API.
Private pages use a login guard.
Reset email works end to end.

chapters.title: Recipe: CRUD with ownership
chapters.subtitle: List, detail, create, edit and delete
chapters.summary: A full CRUD flow with the security detail most tutorials skip: every read and write is scoped to the owner.
chapters.quick_answer: Use generic views for the five pages, override `get_queryset()` to scope by owner, and use `LoginRequiredMixin` before the view. A delete confirmation is a GET page that posts to a DELETE view.

sections.title: List and detail
sections.body: The list and detail views share one scoped queryset. Another user's object becomes a 404.

sections.title: Create, update and delete
sections.body: Set the owner on create, scope update/delete to the owner, and redirect after success.

sections.title: URLs and templates
sections.body: The delete page must submit a POST, not delete on GET. Include CSRF.
sections.code:
urlpatterns = [ path("", PostList.as_view(), name="list"), path("new/", PostCreate.as_view(), name="create"), path("/", PostDetail.as_view(), name="detail"), path("/edit/", PostUpdate.as_view(), name="update"), path("/delete/", PostDelete.as_view(), name="delete"), ]
{% csrf_token %}

Delete “{{ object.title }}”?

pitfalls: Returning 403 when a 404 would not leak existence.
checklist: Reads and writes are scoped to the owner.
Delete is a POST with CSRF.

chapters.title: Recipe: search & filters
chapters.subtitle: Query params, Q objects and pagination
chapters.summary: A search page that handles an empty query, combines filters and paginates without losing the query string.
chapters.quick_answer: Read a small, validated set of query parameters, build a `Q` object, apply an allowlisted sort, paginate, and preserve the query string in pagination links.

sections.title: Build the queryset
sections.body: Never pass raw query params into `order_by` or field names. Validate against an allowlist.

sections.title: View and pagination
sections.body: Paginate the filtered queryset and keep the other params in the pager links.
sections.note: A paginator with an unordered queryset can repeat rows. Always `order_by()` before paginating.

sections.title: Empty states and performance
sections.body: An empty query should show a useful default, not an error. A search page is a common N+1 source; select/prefetch what the template renders.
sections.note: Measure query count with `assertNumQueries`; a search page with authors and categories often hides N+1.

pitfalls: Losing the query string on page 2.
Searching a huge text column without an index.
checklist: The page has a stable query count.
Empty and no-query states are designed.

chapters.title: Recipe: image upload
chapters.subtitle: Validate, store and serve a private image
chapters.summary: An upload flow with the security basics: size/type validation, a generated filename, private storage and a permission-checked download.
chapters.quick_answer: Use a `ModelForm` with `ImageField`, pass `request.FILES`, validate size/type, re-encode with Pillow, store privately, and serve through a view that checks ownership.

sections.title: Model and form
sections.body: Store the file key, not the raw path. Generate a filename and keep the original name only for display.

sections.title: View and template
sections.body: Pass both POST and FILES. Login is required; the profile is fetched for the current user.

sections.title: Serve privately
sections.body: Do not expose `MEDIA_URL` for private avatars. Stream through a view with an ownership check, or redirect to a short-lived signed URL.
sections.note: A public avatar can be served from a CDN; a private document cannot. Decide per field.

pitfalls: Passing only `request.POST` and losing the file.
Trusting the filename or content type.
Loading the whole image into memory for a thumbnail.

chapters.title: Recipe: CSV export
chapters.subtitle: A safe, streaming download in one view
chapters.summary: The smallest correct CSV export: scoped queryset, streamed rows, safe cells and a filename.
chapters.quick_answer: Stream rows from an iterator, escape cells that start with `=+-@`, set `Content-Disposition: attachment`, and scope the query to the current user/tenant.

sections.title: The view
sections.body: Use an `Echo` adapter so `csv.writer` can write to the streaming response.

sections.title: Escape formula injection
sections.body: A cell starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` can become a spreadsheet formula. Prefix it.
sections.code:
DANGEROUS = ("=", "+", "-", "@", "\t", "\r")

def safe_cell(value):
    text = str(value)
    return "'" + text if text.startswith(DANGEROUS) else text
sections.note: This changes the displayed value for a legitimate negative number. Decide per column whether to escape or format as a number.

sections.title: Large exports
sections.body: If the file takes minutes, enqueue a job, store it and send a short-lived link. The request should not occupy a worker.
sections.code:
@shared_task
def build_export(job_id):
    job = ExportJob.objects.get(pk=job_id)
    path = f"exports/{job.pk}.csv"
    with default_storage.open(path, "w") as handle:
        write_orders_csv(handle, job.user_id)
    job.file.name = path
    job.status = "ready"
    job.save(update_fields=["file", "status"])
sections.note: Store the user/tenant scope in the job row. Do not rely on request state inside a worker.

pitfalls: Building the whole CSV in memory.
Exporting every row regardless of tenant/user.
A long export inside the request.
checklist: Large exports run as a job.

chapters.title: Recipe: transactional email
chapters.subtitle: Send, queue and test a receipt
chapters.summary: A production-shaped email flow: a template, a queued send, a retry policy and a test that asserts the message.
chapters.quick_answer: Render subject/body from templates, send in a worker after commit, retry only transient failures, and use the locmem backend in tests.

sections.title: Compose
sections.body: Keep the subject and body in templates so translations and design changes do not touch Python.
sections.code:
from django.core.mail import EmailMultiAlternatives
from django.template.loader import render_to_string

def build_receipt(order):
    context = {"order": order}
    subject = render_to_string("email/receipt_subject.txt", context).strip()
    text = render_to_string("email/receipt.txt", context)
    html = render_to_string("email/receipt.html", context)
    message = EmailMultiAlternatives(subject, text, None, [order.customer.email])
    message.attach_alternative(html, "text/html")
    return message

sections.title: Queue after commit
sections.body: The worker should not see an order that the transaction has not committed. Pass the order id.

sections.title: Test
sections.body: Use the locmem backend and assert the recipient and subject. A reset/receipt link should be tested end to end.
sections.note: `TestCase` wraps the test in a transaction, so use `captureOnCommitCallbacks(execute=True)` for `on_commit` sends.

pitfalls: Testing with a real SMTP server.
checklist: Transient failures retry with a limit.

chapters.title: Recipe: JSON API
chapters.subtitle: A scoped DRF endpoint from zero
chapters.summary: A minimal but production-shaped DRF endpoint: serializer, viewset, router, scoped queryset and a test.
chapters.quick_answer: Define a `ModelSerializer`, a `ModelViewSet` with `get_queryset()` scoped to the user, register it on a router, and require authentication. Paginate and version the URL.

sections.title: Serializer and viewset
sections.body: List fields explicitly and make server-controlled fields read-only.

sections.title: Router and URLs
sections.body: The router generates list/detail routes. Version the prefix.
sections.code:
router = DefaultRouter()
router.register("posts", PostViewSet, basename="post")

urlpatterns = [
    path("api/v1/", include(router.urls)),
]
sections.note: A router is a convenience, not a requirement. Use explicit paths when the URL shape is not CRUD.

sections.title: Test
sections.body: Prove authentication, creation and cross-user isolation.

pitfalls: Changing the response shape without a version.

chapters.title: Recipe: first deploy
chapters.subtitle: Settings, release script, health and rollback
chapters.summary: A launch checklist you can execute: production settings, a repeatable release, a health check and a rollback.
chapters.quick_answer: Set `DEBUG=False`, real secrets and hosts; run migrate + collectstatic once; serve with Gunicorn/WhiteNoise; add health/readiness; keep the previous image for rollback.

sections.title: Production settings
sections.body: These are the minimums. Keep values in the environment.
sections.code:
DEBUG = False
SECRET_KEY = os.environ["DJANGO_SECRET_KEY"]
ALLOWED_HOSTS = os.environ["DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS"].split(",")
CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = os.environ.get("DJANGO_CSRF_TRUSTED_ORIGINS", "").split(",")

SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True
CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True
SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000
X_FRAME_OPTIONS = "DENY"

DATABASES = {"default": dj_database_url.config(conn_max_age=600)}

sections.title: Release script
sections.body: Run migrations once, collect static, check and restart. Keep it idempotent.
sections.code:
set -e
pip install -r requirements.txt
python manage.py migrate --noinput
python manage.py collectstatic --noinput
python manage.py check --deploy
gunicorn config.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 --workers 3 --timeout 30
sections.note: Do not run `migrate` from every web worker at boot; they will race.

sections.title: Health and rollback
sections.body: A shallow health check proves the process is alive; readiness proves dependencies work. Keep the previous image and a database backup.
sections.note: After deploy, watch error rate, p95 latency and queue depth. Roll back before debugging in production if the blast radius is growing.

chapters.title: Recipe: background job
chapters.subtitle: Enqueue, retry and observe one job
chapters.summary: A single job that is safe to retry: enqueue after commit, pass an id, dedupe and log.
chapters.quick_answer: Define a task that takes an id, write the job intent in the transaction, enqueue with `on_commit`, and make the task idempotent with a dedupe key.

sections.title: The task
sections.body: The task fetches its own data and records success. It should be safe to run twice.

sections.title: Enqueue after commit
sections.body: The row must exist before the worker reads it.
sections.code:
with transaction.atomic():
    invoice = Invoice.objects.create(order=order, total=order.total)
    transaction.on_commit(lambda: sync_invoice.delay(invoice.pk))

sections.title: Observe
sections.body: Log the job id, invoice id, attempt and outcome. Alert on a growing queue and failures.
sections.code:
logger.info("invoice.sync", extra={"invoice_id": invoice_id, "attempt": self.request.retries})
# Metrics: queue depth, duration, failures, oldest job age
sections.note: A task with no logs and no metrics is invisible until a customer complains.

chapters.title: Recipe: tenant scoping
chapters.subtitle: Resolve, scope and test one tenant boundary
chapters.summary: A minimal shared-schema tenant flow: membership, middleware, scoped manager and a leak test.
chapters.quick_answer: Add `tenant` to every owned model, resolve membership in middleware, filter at the manager/service layer, and test that user A cannot read B's rows.

sections.title: Model and middleware
sections.body: Resolve the tenant from the host, verify membership, and attach it to the request.

sections.title: Scope the queryset
sections.body: Every tenant-owned model gets a `tenant` FK. Services take the tenant explicitly; views pass `request.tenant`.

sections.title: Test the leak
sections.body: Two tenants, two users, one object. User A must not read or mutate B's row.
sections.note: Test the admin, exports and background jobs too. The view is not the only path to the data.

pitfalls: Filtering by tenant only in the view.
Forgetting `tenant` on a new owned model.
An admin changelist that shows every tenant.
A missing tenant returning all rows.
checklist: Owned models carry a tenant FK.
